title: "Show me the market"
hookLine: offered half his brother's wealth, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf asks only to be shown the market (Bukhari)

cards: Two strangers, made brothers. When the emigrants arrived in Medina with almost nothing, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, paired them up with the people of the city. Newcomers were given local brothers.

Bukhari keeps one of those pairings in the newcomer's own words. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from Mecca, is paired with Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', from Medina. And Sa'd, almost at once, makes him an enormous offer.

teach.b: Sa'd says, in Abd al-Rahman's telling: I am the wealthiest of the Ansar. I will divide my wealth in half, and half is yours. Weigh that.
Not a meal or a loan: half of everything, to a man he has just met, because the Prophet called them brothers. Abd al-Rahman answers, in effect: I have no need of that.
Is there a market here where trade goes on? Sa'd tells him: the market of Qaynuqa. The next morning Abd al-Rahman is there.

teach.h: CURD AND BUTTER, DAY AFTER DAY.
teach.b: He buys and sells dried curd and clarified butter, small goods, and keeps going back, day after day. Before long, Bukhari says, he turns up with a trace of yellow perfume on him, the sign of a bridegroom.
He has earned enough to marry. Neither man is the hero alone. Sa'd's generosity is real and total: he offered half, and meant it.

Abd al-Rahman's refusal isn't pride. He answers with thanks, and with a blessing on Sa'd's family and wealth. What he asks for instead is a door: not the money, but the place where money is honestly made.

teach.h: ONE GIVES, ONE PROTECTS THE GIVER.
teach.b: The other protects the giver, and keeps his own dignity.

how: Muslims tell the story of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' when speaking of the brotherhood (mu'akhah) between the emigrants and the Ansar, and of earning an honest living.

o: the market where Abd al-Rahman began to trade
the clan of Sa'd, who offered half his wealth
the yellow perfume worn by a new bridegroom

games.q: show me the market — tap the pairs.
p: where he went the next morning

s: Abd al-Rahman took half of Sa'd's wealth to start out
he thanked him, refused, and asked for the market.
the Prophet paired emigrants with people of Medina as brothers
Abd al-Rahman was paired with Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'.
he started out trading small goods like curd and butter
Bukhari names dried curd and clarified butter.

games.q: you've arrived with nothing. your new brother offers you half of everything he owns. what do you say?
o: thank you; is there a market here?
I'll take a loan, not a gift.
games.why: Abd al-Rahman blessed Sa'd's family and wealth, refused, and asked for the market. by the next morning he was trading.

practice: Think about your work, paid or unpaid, and the way you earn what you have, and let yourself be glad of one place where it's honest and clean.
Then notice one place that could be cleaner, a shortcut, an exaggeration, a corner cut, and simply see it, without arguing with it. If you pray, you can ask Allah to bless what you earn.

wordCard.voice: Qaynuqa, the market Sa'd sent him to, where Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf earned his own way instead of taking half his new brother's wealth. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: 'the market'; Abd al-Rahman asks to be shown the market.

carryVoice: Your line: a trace of yellow perfume. He asked for the door, and walked through it himself. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2048 (Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: brotherhood with Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'; offer of half his wealth; the market of Qaynuqa; dried curd and butter; the trace of saffron)
